source.inputPreservation: Read-only; no crop, edit, conversion or replacement.

fig-152.composition: A single apparatus view: round-faced instrument at left, two separate upright plates with separate supports at right, two connecting leads, and a thin outlined slab/frame in the lower-right foreground.
fig-152.pixelRegionConvention: Approximate [left, top, right, bottom] image-pixel locating boxes, origin top-left. These identify visible regions only; they are not physical dimensions, calibrated measurements or committed renderer coordinates.

sourceFacts.observation: The instrument has a complete, thick, nearly circular outer face/rim, including the left, upper, right and lower perimeter. Its interior is mostly open white space, with several independent fine-stroke groups. The lower rim meets the supporting stem; the lower-right rim carries a protruding connection/tab.
sourceFacts.certainty: Visible structure; exact circularity is not a printed fact.

sourceFacts.observation: A thin, approximately vertical central rod runs from the top terminal into the face and down nearly to the bottom, ending in a small dark rounded mark. A much heavier diagonal indicator runs from the lower-left interior through the central junction toward the upper-right interior. Preserve both sides of that diagonal indicator and its intersection with the central rod, not merely an isolated upper-right arrow.
sourceFacts.certainty: Stroke topology and visible orientation; no quantitative deflection or physical reading.

sourceFacts.observation: The upper-left face contains a cluster of fine, roughly parallel diagonal strokes rising toward the right. Some meet or merge into the dark outer rim and the central rod. This cluster is separate from the main diagonal indicator and must not disappear when the old ink is regularized.
sourceFacts.certainty: Cluster existence, direction and location are visible; its exact stroke count and purpose are ambiguous.

sourceFacts.observation: A short oblique mark appears on the lower-left interior above a fan of short graduation-like strokes near the lower-left/bottom arc. The short strokes change orientation along the arc. Additional thin diagonal strokes occur in the lower-right interior near the rim. Retain these separate fine-stroke families and the small rod-end mark.
sourceFacts.certainty: Visible fine-stroke groups; no readable numerals, units, zero mark, calibrated divisions or reliable exact scale count.

sourceFacts.observation: The top lead meets the small dark terminal above the instrument face, aligned with the central rod. A second lead meets the protruding lower-right body/rim terminal; the body also has dark lower rim/tab details. The two external contacts are at different positions and must remain distinct.
sourceFacts.certainty: Two visible external attachment locations; internal electrical construction is not shown.

sourceFacts.observation: Below the full instrument rim is a substantial vertical neck/stem with narrow internal/edge strokes, broadening into a dark splayed tripod-like base with projecting limbs and foot ends. Retain the visible support silhouette and overlapping limb contours rather than replacing the entire instrument with a floating dial or a single line pedestal.
sourceFacts.certainty: Visible stem and splayed base. Do not invent a hidden leg or assign measured lengths to overlapping limbs.

sourceFacts.observation: Two separate tall, narrow, closed oval/ellipse-like plate outlines stand side by side. Each has its own upper and lower curved contour and near-vertical sides. Their adjacent inner contours come very close in this projection and include a dark narrow central region; they must still read as two plates, not one merged oval or a single filled block.
sourceFacts.certainty: Exactly two visible plates. The oval outlines are a projected appearance, not proof of elliptical physical plates or a measurable gap.

sourceFacts.observation: The left plate has a horizontal mounting arm extending left toward its own upright post. A small rounded/outlined end or collar is visible at the plate-side arm. The post has a dark cap, narrow double-edge vertical strokes, collars/side-knob details around its upper portion, and a broad splayed base with visible feet and a small projecting upturned detail. Preserve the mounting arm, fine post edges and collar outlines independently.
sourceFacts.certainty: Visible support and attachment topology; not a measurement or a claim about insulating material.

sourceFacts.observation: The right plate has its own horizontal arm extending right to a separate capped upright post. A rounded dark/outlined top contact, narrow double-edge post, upper collar/side-knob details, and splayed base with projecting feet/details are visible. It remains a distinct support from the left plate stand, even where the curved lead crosses the post.
sourceFacts.certainty: Visible separate support and contact topology; not a claim that the two stands are electrically connected.

sourceFacts.observation: One continuous solid lead leaves the instrument top terminal, rises into a high inverted-U arch above the face, descends toward the right, then curves through a shallow low section into the upper attachment region of the left plate support/arm. The entire arch is present and within the source crop.
sourceFacts.certainty: Visible lead route and end regions. No current direction, polarity, wire length or voltage is printed.

sourceFacts.observation: A second continuous solid lead leaves the instrument lower-right terminal, runs rightward in a shallow bow below the plates, then rises diagonally, loops outward to the right of the right post and returns to the right plate's upper contact region. Preserve the full long bow, rising return and short outer loop; do not truncate it at a post crossing.
sourceFacts.certainty: Visible lead route and distinct endpoints; no grounded-end symbol or circuit source is drawn.

sourceFacts.observation: The lower lead passes across the left post low down and across the right post on its rising route. These projected crossings are not accompanied by a separate explicit junction dot. The intended visible terminal meeting is up at the right arm/post contact. Keep separate paths and do not turn intermediate post crossings or the nearly touching plate contours into new electrical contacts.
sourceFacts.certainty: Pixel crossings without an explicit separate junction mark; circuit interpretation awaits frozen prose.

sourceFacts.observation: An oblique, roughly quadrilateral, unfilled slab/table-frame outline lies below and in front of the plate stands. Its top/back edge rises toward the right stand area, its right edge runs to the far-right corner, and the long front edge and left return close the outline. A closely spaced second edge/short thickness stroke is visible especially at the left/front corner and adjoining edge. Preserve the thin frame/thickness strokes and its foreground position.
sourceFacts.certainty: Visible thin slab/frame. Pixels alone do not establish material, dimensions or table construction. No legs are visible, and it is not a third upright plate between the two plates.

sourceFacts.observation: There is no visible textual label, mathematical variable, numeral, unit, polarity symbol, dimension line, arrowhead denoting direction or caption inside this crop. The instrument contains fine graduation-like ink but no legible printed values.
sourceFacts.certainty: No source-provided numerical readings or named diagram labels to carry into the modern figure.

uncalibratedIllustrativePositions: All approximate pixel boxes are finding aids, not physical measurements.
The indicator's visible lower-left/upper-right orientation is retained qualitatively; its angle is not converted into volts, charge, capacitance or a numbered division.
Plate projected aspect ratios, spacing, parallel-looking orientation and stand positions are not calibrated physical geometry.
Lead curvature, crossing locations, arch height and relative lengths are illustrative; only complete routes and attachment topology are source requirements.
Tripod limbs, post widths, contact sizes and slab perspective have no printed dimensions.
Regularized modern curves, clean rim circularity, minor contour spacing and thicker mobile-safe fine strokes must be declared as modern drawing choices.

fineStrokeAmbiguityPolicy.rule: Preserve all confidently distinguishable fine stroke families and individual strokes from this one observation. Never invent an exact division count, uniform graduation pattern, numerals, zero reference or calibration. Ambiguous merged ink remains recorded as a cluster, not a certified count. If frozen prose requires reading a numerical scale not visible here, stop for Main instead of filling it in.

permittedAfterFreeze: Clean deterministic finite geometry with semantic ink/muted/paper roles.
Noncalibrated contour regularization that keeps both plates, both wires, contacts, face details, supports and foreground frame.
Fine stroke widths sufficient to survive 331 px display, without coalescing separate strokes.
